utility.notes: Given as the run's input parameter; directly confirmed as the electric/gas franchise utility for the City of San Diego via the City's own official page. SDG&E is the distribution/interconnection utility of record; see generation_supplier for the separate default generation supplier.

value.name: San Diego Community Power (SDCP)
value.notes: The City of San Diego is a founding member/customer of San Diego Community Power, a joint-powers Community Choice Aggregator that purchases/generates electricity on customers' behalf. SDG&E remains the transmission/distribution entity and delivers the electricity SDCP procures. Customers receive one bill from SDG&E, with SDCP's generation charge appearing as a line item rather than a separate bill.

Direct page content could not be rendered (HTTP 403) this session; confidence reflects domain-level/structural confirmation rather than a rendered explicit quote, the same limitation encountered for county fields in every prior pilot record.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Center for Sustainable Energy (CSE), on behalf of SDG&E, under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. This is the same statewide SGIP tier used in the PG&E-territory pilot records; SDG&E-territory administration is confirmed to be handled by CSE rather than SDG&E directly.

value.name: SGIP - Equity Resiliency
value.administrator: Center for Sustainable Energy (CSE), on behalf of SDG&E, under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Incentive of $1,000/kWh for IOU residential or non-residential customers. Source states this rate is/was 'available through 2025.'
value.eligibility: IOU residential or non-residential customers meeting Equity Resiliency criteria (e.g. high fire-threat district, medical baseline). Specific San Diego eligibility not independently confirmed this session.

battery_programs.notes: Unlike the PG&E-territory records (which reused the same figures without independently re-confirming the administrator), this record independently verified via CPUC's own page that SDG&E's SGIP administrator is specifically 'SDG&E – Via Center for Sustainable Energy (CSE)' — confirmed NOT to be SDG&E directly, and NOT the same generic administrator description used for PG&E. Rate figures ($1,100/kWh, $1,000/kWh) are the same statewide CPUC-set SGIP budgets, not utility-specific numbers, so reuse of the figures themselves is warranted; only the administrator attribution required independent verification, which was done. Same 'through 2025' elapsed-window caveat as prior records applies to the Equity Resiliency tier.

value: After final inspection approval for all related City permits, the City notifies SDG&E; the system is not approved to energize until SDG&E gives its own approval
inspection_steps.notes: Quoted directly from IB-301: 'After receiving final inspection approval for all related City of San Diego Permits, San Diego Gas and Electric (SDG&E) will be notified. The system is not approved to energize until SDG&E approval is obtained.' This is a genuine two-authority sign-off (City then SDG&E), distinct from the single-authority processes in the PG&E/Ava-territory and PWP records.

timeline_days.notes: IB-301 does not specify a standard turnaround/timeline for residential review. It mentions an 'Express Plan Check' service (1.5x regular fees) for faster review, but explicitly states this expedited option is 'not available for single-family/duplex/ADU projects' — the exact category most residential solar falls into — so it does not provide a usable residential timeline either.
